proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: for two objects over T, isomorphic restrictions force g o h = g' o h, so Isom maps to the equalizer of g, g', a scheme by representability of the diagonal of B; replacing T by the equalizer one assumes g = g'; after base change to T, restrict B to the intersection of the two open loci W and W' (any isomorphism forces both factorizations, since over fibres a quasi-isomorphism kills positive Exts), where the four SheafHom functors H, H', I, I' are affine finitely presented algebraic spaces by the negative-Ext vanishing lemma, and the proposition-isom argument presents Isom(E, E') as a fibre product of these (source lines 5433-5489)

core_obligations: Equalizer reduction (proof lines 5434-5448): Isom(x, y) maps to the equalizer of g and g', a scheme; replace T by it to assume g = g'.
Base change to T (proof lines 5449-5455): reformulate as Isom(E, E') for E, E' satisfying conditions (1), (2).
Restrict to W cap W' (proof lines 5456-5472): an isomorphism forces factorization through both opens; over the intersection the Hom functor H is an affine fp algebraic space, likewise H', I, I'.
Fibre product presentation (proof lines 5473-5489): repeating the proposition-isom argument gives Isom(E, E') = (H' x_B H) x_{c, I x_B I', sigma} B, an algebraic space.
proof_roadmap: Descend to the equalizer of g, g' (proof lines 5434-5448).
Reformulate after base change to T (proof lines 5449-5455).
Cut down to W cap W' and note the four Hom spaces are affine fp (proof lines 5456-5477).
Present Isom as a fibre product (proof lines 5478-5489).
